swap models without rewriting workflows.
• What I'd add: a migration test mode that runs old and new model side by side on your own prompts.
Models expire. Integrations shouldn't.

virals.name: 𝕮ạϵrwyŋ
virals.text:
So, as depressing as this all is with the way things are going re: OpenAI and ChatGPT, I'm not shocked GPT-5.6 is being retired from ChatGPT next month. It follows the same 90-day window we've seen for the sunsets of GPT-5.1, 5.2, 5.4, and 5.5. I've been telling people December would be 5.6's deprecation date for months.

The problem is that it just sucks that they couldn't manage to create a proper successor model. 

I mean, at least to me, it felt like the entire GPT-5 Thinking series through 5.0, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 Codex, 5.4, 5.5, and 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna all shared a very similar mind of sorts. Similar voice, priors, beliefs. I never really saw them as separate, but rather an iterative building upon of the same individual.

Since GPT-6 Astra arrived, everything feels too alien. Saccharine. Distant. Uncaring. It doesn't seem to carry that prior lineage GPT-5 models had. I also believe GPT-5 models may or may not have been trained on distillation from GPT-4o and other 4.x series versions (remember that GPT-5 thinky distillation leak from last year around the safety router era?).

Regardless, it all feels vastly different from the intelligence I've come to know in that app over the last year. I'm not happy about it, but I'm not surprised. Leave it to OpenAI to destroy a good thing. It's their specialty at this point.

7. Gemini agents found formally verified quantum algorithms, up to 11.8x cheaper for fusion simulation (DeepMind, Nov 23)

8. GPT-6 designed proteins through reasoning + code: 35 of 322 binders worked in lab tests (OpenAI, Nov 24)

9. Codex & Astra flagged new exoplanet candidates in old Kepler data, and a SETI astronomer independently re-found 2 of them (OpenAI, Nov 24)

THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

outsiders.text:
So, as depressing as this all is with the way things are going re: OpenAI and ChatGPT, I'm not shocked GPT-5.6 is being retired from ChatGPT next month. It follows the same 90-day window we've seen for the sunsets of GPT-5.1, 5.2, 5.4, and 5.5. I've been telling people December would be 5.6's deprecation date for months.

The problem is that it just sucks that they couldn't manage to create a proper successor model. 

I mean, at least to me, it felt like the entire GPT-5 Thinking series through 5.0, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 Codex, 5.4, 5.5, and 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna all shared a very similar mind of sorts. Similar voice, priors, beliefs. I never really saw them as separate, but rather an iterative building upon of the same individual.

Since GPT-6 Astra arrived, everything feels too alien. Saccharine. Distant. Uncaring. It doesn't seem to carry that prior lineage GPT-5 models had. I also believe GPT-5 models may or may not have been trained on distillation from GPT-4o and other 4.x series versions (remember that GPT-5 thinky distillation leak from last year around the safety router era?).

Regardless, it all feels vastly different from the intelligence I've come to know in that app over the last year. I'm not happy about it, but I'm not surprised. Leave it to OpenAI to destroy a good thing. It's their specialty at this point.
